title: event
description: One event in the lossless event codec (internal/agent/eventcodec.go, codec version 1): an event notification's event, verbatim, and the shape every leaf payload of the protocol has. Every key but type is omitted at its zero value, so absent means zero; a pointer's presence is kept (an object that is present and empty is not an absent one); times are RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, in UTC. A client ignores keys and event types it does not know.

type.description: The event's kind. A client ignores a kind it does not know.

text.description: A text, thought or user chunk; a title (meta).

mode.description: The mode an agent-initiated meta reports.

agent.description: The sub-agent the event belongs to; absent for the main transcript.

subagentChange.description: spawned, progress, finished, or removed: a retained row the session has dropped, which a client drops too.

replayed.description: The event came from a session/load replay.

keptPlanning.description: On a done whose stop reason is cancelled: the turn ended because its plan was answered keep planning (claude), not because anyone cancelled it, so no cancelled note is drawn.

time.description: A time: RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, in UTC.

toolEdited.description: What an edit call that completed reported changing (ToolEdited).

toolOutput.description: A tool's output. exitCode is present, 0 included, whenever the tool reported one.

task.description: A task tool's sub-agent details; its presence, even empty, marks the tool a task.

todo.description: One todo: status is pending, in_progress, completed or cancelled.

permission.description: A permission request: every offered option verbatim, duplicate kinds included. Answer with the exact optionId.

permissionOption.description: One offered option: kind is ACP's (allow_once, allow_always, reject_once, reject_always).

questionItem.description: One question of a question request.

allowText.description: The question also takes a free-text answer of the user's own (answer text): claude's "Other" box. No other provider sets it.

required.description: The question must be answered with an option id whenever the ask is answered, and the ask cannot be skipped: a claude form's required. No other provider sets it.

answers.description: Each question's id to the option ids chosen. A null list is not an empty one: null is written for a nil list, [] for an empty one.

answerText.description: Each question's id to its free-text answer, for a question with allowText.

subagent.description: One sub-agent roster row (SubagentInfo): status is running, completed, failed or cancelled.

retained.description: The session alone decides when this row goes, and says so with a removed subagentChange; a client does not evict it by its own finished-row cap (claude's rows). Absent is false.

noCancel.description: This child cannot be stopped on its own (a claude child whose capabilities grant no cancel): its row offers no stop, though the session has session.subagent.cancel. Absent is false.

queued.description: One queued prompt (QueuedPrompt): a queue event's row, and every queue row the protocol carries.

command.description: A plugin command or skill craze expanded into the prompt it is about to send.

pluginCommand.description: A plugin command or skill: kind is command, skill or agent.

foreignTurn.description: One end of a turn the agent ran on its own: running on its start, absent on its end. reason is on both ends when the agent gave one. An end may say how the turn ended: cancelled, or err for a failed turn.

reason.description: Why the agent started the turn: an open string, not an enum. Absent ("") is grok's interjection fallback; subagent_wake is the native session delivering a background sub-agent's result, job_wake one delivering background commands' results; background is claude running a cycle of its own (a background command's or a sub-agent's wake, or a steer that started a turn); compaction is claude compacting its context while idle. A client reads a value it does not know as absent.

cancelled.description: On an end: a user cancel ended the turn. Absent is false.

err.description: On an end: the turn failed, and why — kind (one of the kinds in the CLI reference) and message. A failed foreign turn settles as a failed turn. Absent when it did not fail.

turn.description: One end of an engine-driven turn (TurnInfo): phase started (with text and origin: submit, drain or send_now) or ended (with its stop reason, and errClass/err and kind/retryable/status/provider_code for a failure; synthetic for an ending the wire never produced; next, the successor turn this settlement started; pending, the rows still queued; cause, what began a close's ending).

kind.description: What the failure said of itself where it happened, one of the kinds in the CLI reference; absent from a host that predates it, which a reader takes for unknown.

retryable.description: A fresh turn may succeed. Absent is false.

status.description: The provider's HTTP status; absent for none. An ACP agent's JSON-RPC code is not one.

provider_code.description: The provider's own short name for the failure; absent for none.

cause.description: On a synthetic ended whose stopReason is closing: what began the session's close, one of stop, signal, idle, exit_after_turn, lost_owner or overage. Absent from a host that predates it, and when a terminal closed its own session.

ask.description: One ask's ending (AskUpdate): kind is permission, question or plan; outcome answered, cancelled, turn_ended, closing or automatic; by whose doing (client, call, cancel, turn, close, policy, provider, withdrawn — the agent took its request back, claude's $/cancel_request — unavailable). body is set only when no opening was ever published.

cancelled.description: A question cancelled rather than answered (answer cancel): claude's Esc, which aborts the tool that asked.

askBody.description: An ask's opening exactly as offered: one of the three, in the shape its own opening event has.

state.description: A state delta (StateDelta): the sections of the shared state one event changed, each in full. A section that is absent was not touched; one that is present was set, to "" or {} included. The delta's seq is the change's revision.

webSearch.description: The web search section (WebSearchState; native only, absent for every ACP session and never null): the open turn's web tally, cumulative — each delta carries the whole tally so far and replaces what a client holds, never adds to it. It names no turn: a client stamps it with the turn running in the log as it arrives (a running foreign bracket's id first, else the engine turn's), and a native session sends it only inside a turn's window. searches and fetches are the calls the web service handled, whatever their outcome; failed those that returned an error; urls the URLs of successful results (a search's result URLs in order, a fetch's requested URL when its page had text), key scrubbed and redacted, each at most 500 bytes, distinct, first seen first, at most 100; urlsTruncated, a URL cut or a distinct one dropped. Each member is omitted when zero, empty or false. Completion-window activity accounting, not provenance of an answer; the counters are incarnation-local.

webStatus.description: The web status section (WebStatusState; native only, absent for every ACP session and never null or {}): the session's web search as it stands now — provider, the provider's id ("exa"); key, where the key the session sends came from ("keyless", "env" or "stored"); consent, where its consent stands ("allowed", "allowed for this session", "disabled", "declined" or "undecided"); and its call totals: searches and fetches the calls its web service handled, failed those that returned an error, rateLimited those of them that were a rate limit after every retry, retries the attempts made again after a rate limit, sub-agents' calls included. Session-wide, never stamped with a turn: each delta carries the whole of it and replaces what a client holds. A native session that offered the web tools sends one after every call its web service handled, when a key stored mid-session is taken up, and at its first turn. The totals are incarnation-local: a reload's session starts them from zero. Always every key.

usage.description: The usage section (UsageState; native, claude, and codex, absent for every cursor, grok and antigravity session and never null or {}): the estimated size in tokens of what the session's next request sends (contextTokens) and the context the model it goes to works within (contextWindow: its default_context when that is below its context window, else the window; 0 when the window is unknown), and what the session has spent — in the turn the report followed (after a load, the last turn the stored session recorded) and in all (session). Always every key but the plan's, which are claude's and codex's and optional: plan, the subscription ("max", "prolite", …); window, the window of the plan's latest limit report (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_overage_included, overage, or a compact duration like 24h; an open string); windowUtilization, that window's use from 0 to 1, written exactly when window is (0 when the report carried none); resetsAt, when it resets; and model, the model the agent's last usage report said it ran. A claude or codex session's spend is tokens only: costPicoUsd 0 and unpriced true.

catalog.description: The catalog section (CatalogState; native, antigravity, and codex; absent for cursor, grok, and claude sessions, absent for native and antigravity until the list first changes, and emitted on codex at initial install and whenever effort/model updates rebuild switchEffort; never null or {}): every model the session offers now, in the picker's order, and the revision of that list, always written. The revision only ever grows within one incarnation, and a client never applies a revision lower than the one it holds: an older list never replaces a newer one, whatever order a reconnect or a replay brings them in. The session holds the list to these bounds where it builds it, the info document's catalogs.models with it: at most 512 models, in the picker's order with the running model among them; each name at most 128 bytes, cut with an ellipsis; a model whose id would be over 256 bytes is not offered, an id never cut; a model's effort facts at most 8 levels of at most 32 bytes each, or none.

catalogModel.description: One model the session offers: the info document's catalog model (info.json's model), id and name always written, recent its rank in the native provider's model memory and absent for a model not remembered, and its effort facts where the session capability effortFacts is true — efforts, the levels it offers in order, absent for a model with no effort control; defaultEffort; and switchEffort, the effort a switch to it lands on — each absent otherwise.

spend.description: A sum of usage and its cost (Spend): the tokens as the provider billed them — input is the uncached input, reasoning is part of output — and costPicoUsd, the priced part's cost in picodollars (10^-12 USD; $1 is 1000000000000), exact. unpriced says some usage in it had no price in craze's model table: its tokens are counted and it added no cost. Always every key.

config.description: The provider's config options, in full; {} for none.

commands.description: The agent's slash commands, in full; {} for none.

plugins.description: The plugin commands and skills craze found, in full; {} for none.

slash.description: The slash catalog section (SlashCatalog; a session whose capabilities.slashCatalog is true): every / row the session offers, in the order a menu lists them, in full; {} for none. A delta that carries commands or plugins restates it beside them, and one that carries it alone is a change of the disk skills the host scanned. Absent from every delta of a session that does not publish it, and never null. Nothing in it is cut: a row's action fields (every key but description, run.argHint and run.reason) are what a client acts on. A decoder reads it row by row: a row that does not match slashItem, or whose name is not one token, is dropped alone, and a slash or items value that is not an object or an array is a section with no rows — never a reason to reject the section or the event. craze writes neither.

slashItem.description: One slash row: name is the token without its /, always written, never empty and never holding whitespace or a control character (a row whose name is not one token is dropped by a decoder). source is builtin, agent, plugin or skill; plugin and qualified are a plugin row's, qualified only where it differs from name (the second spelling the row answers to); requires is what the row needs: the session capability stop or aside, or effort, the client's own reading of the snapshot (an effort option for the current model); a client shows the row only where that is true — a requires row claims no name, so a client keeps, per name, the first row it shows; whileWorking says the row runs while a turn is running rather than being refused (absent false; a prompt row omits it, it queues). The values of source, requires and every run key are not closed here: a client hides a row with a value it does not know, and a later host may add one.

slashRun.description: What running a slash row does, by kind: prompt (send /name and its argument as a session.prompt's text), method (call method — session.setTitle, session.set or session.stop — the argument filling the param it names, session.set sending setting verbatim), picker (open the picker it names: model), aside (ask a side question, session.aside, the argument filling param), local (the client's own action it names: help, clear, tasks, theme, connect) or unavailable (it cannot run here, and selecting it reports reason). arg is absent for none, optional or required; argHint is how to show it.

slashSetting.description: session.set's setting object as a method row sends it, verbatim: its kind (mode) and value, a mode already resolved to an id the session advertised.

configOption.description: One config option and its current value.

selectValue.description: One value a select option offers.

commandInfo.description: One slash command the agent advertises.

sendNow.description: The send-now section: armed, its text, the row it re-takes and the turn it replaces; {} when nothing is armed.

replay.description: One end of a session/load replay: phase start or end.

compaction.description: One end of a compaction of a session's context (CompactionInfo; native, and claude's compaction_update): phase started, then ended. reason is auto, manual or overflow, an open string. A native ended one carries tokensBefore, the context's estimated size before it, and either tokensAfter, its estimated size after, or err, why no summary was written; a claude one carries no sizes, only err for one that failed or was cancelled. A native replay carries only the ended one of each stored compaction. The event's agent names the sub-agent whose context it was.

notice.description: A notice the agent sent the user (NoticeInfo; claude only, from Claude Code's notices): severity, the agent's word for it (info, warning, error; an open string), title its headline and description the rest. Either of title and description may be absent, never both. A client draws it as a note.

stepRetry.description: A step's model request failed and is being sent again from the same input (StepRetryInfo; native only): before it produced output, or after, for a transport or server failure. turn and step are the harness's numbers, as a native tool call's id spells them; attempt counts this step's retries from 1, and total the turn's over all its steps. reason is the failure, on one line; delayMs the wait before the next attempt. When discarded is set, the failed attempt's text, thought and tool events are not part of the answer, and no tool of it ran: every one of them on the stream of the event's agent from seq from on, which a reader that holds them retracts.

error.description: An event's error: its message, its class (rpc, closed, agent_exited, agent_exit_status, canceled, deadline_exceeded, auth, model_not_found, context_too_large, empty_step, empty_prompt, harness_closed, provider, other, prompt_cancelled, prompt_in_flight, foreign_turn; a class a later craze wrote is kept as it is) and its code (the JSON-RPC code, HTTP status or exit status, else 0), all three always present; then what it said of itself where it happened, each absent at its zero value.

kind.description: What the failure said of itself where it happened, one of the kinds in the CLI reference; absent from a host that predates it, which a reader takes for unknown.

retryable.description: A fresh turn may succeed. Absent is false.

status.description: The provider's HTTP status; absent for none. An ACP agent's JSON-RPC code is not one.

provider_code.description: The provider's own short name for the failure; absent for none.
